trigger: a reader checks the token-mint docs for who may mint a service-scoped token
summary: The two token-mint arms refuse an engine session on both transports and an MCP-tier session on REST, but the mint docs stated only the owner-or-ManagementGroup:Write rule (also docs-writer F1 and enterprise-readiness 2). FIXED: one sentence each in docs/user-manual/rest-api.md (POST /tokens), docs/user-manual/mcp.md (create_api_token row) and a new bullet in docs/user-manual/authentication.md 'Service-Scoped Tokens'.
classification_rationale: the refusal is stated on the roles routes and in the changelog, not at the mint docs

trigger: a reader of the query_installed_software row looks for the error code of a refused cursor
summary: The row's first cursor sentence listed only the malformed and filter-mismatch cases as kInvalidParams; the ceiling refusal was named only further down the row. FIXED: the first sentence now lists all three. The docs-writer report file was not saved in the run directory; this row is recorded from the run's disposition, so severity_native is null.
classification_rationale: the code was already stated later in the same row

trigger: a reader uses management-groups.md, not rest-api.md, for the role-assignment rules
summary: management-groups.md did not mention the service-scoped, MCP-tier and engine refusals, nor the Operator/Viewer limit on an owner-only DELETE. FIXED: the add, remove and API-table lines now state them.
classification_rationale: the one manual the change left behind

trigger: the sole owner of a group wants to remove their own ITServiceOwner assignment
summary: No documented procedure for an owner stepping down after the DELETE limit. FIXED: the DELETE section says a holder of the global ManagementGroup:Write permission removes an ITServiceOwner row with the same DELETE, and that POST accepts only Operator and Viewer from every caller, so the API does not assign ITServiceOwner to a successor (checked: the only two production callers of ManagementGroupStore::assign_role sit behind that role check). The reporter wrote I4 and derived LOW; recorded as I8 because the 403 is visible and names the limit.
classification_rationale: a new limit with no stated way round it for the legitimate case

trigger: a reader checks the ADR against the rpm query format
summary: The ADR said the rpm format has VENDOR last and the parser takes ten tokens; PACKAGER is now last and the parser takes at least nine (also consistency-auditor C-1). FIXED: the paragraph names kRpmInvQueryFormat, VENDOR then PACKAGER last, at least nine tokens, publisher read as the text before any tab. The reporter wrote I4 and derived LOW; recorded as I8 because no operator action depends on the sentence.
classification_rationale: the sentence contradicted the code after this change

trigger: a group owner calls a roles route or the token mint over REST with an MCP-tier token
summary: A refused owner arm answers the generic 403 'forbidden'; the cause (session class, not membership) is in the docs only (also sre 2). DECLINED for this change: the same refusal answers 'forbidden' on the MCP twins and in their denied audit detail, so a cause on REST alone would split two surfaces this change made identical, and a cause on both is seven handler sites plus tests on each transport. It belongs with the denial audit-row follow-up (compliance-officer F1), which edits these same branches. The manuals now state the cause at the mint and group docs (d1, d3). The reporter wrote I4 and derived LOW; recorded as I8 because the refusal is visible and documented.
classification_rationale: a message improvement the reporter called optional

trigger: an operator reads the release notes for behaviour changes
summary: The fragment described the operator-visible changes after the Windows item. FIXED: reordered to lead with the owner-arm refusals, the owner-only DELETE limit and the cursor ceiling; the Windows and package items follow.
classification_rationale: ordering only; every statement was already present

trigger: junction creation fails after CreateDirectoryW on the Windows test leg
summary: Row R6 said a failed junction build returns before any handle is held; that holds only when CreateDirectoryW fails. A later failure leaks no handle but leaves an empty link directory under the test temp tree. FIXED: R6 now says so. The helper was lifted unchanged and is not edited.
classification_rationale: the ledger row overstated the failure cleanup

trigger: a Windows build rejects the no-reparse open and the plugin logs the cause
summary: The reporter inferred that a plugin image's default spdlog logger may not be the agent's sink. DECLINED on the repo's own measurement: agents/core/src/log_handoff.hpp (MULTI-IMAGE note) and docs/spark-rebuild-baselines/4666-mi1b-windows-registry-verdict.md record ONE shared spdlog registry on Windows (spdlog.dll, measured on MSVC hardware 2026-10-03), the same route 54 other plugin sources use; the runtimes plugin already links spdlog. No code or wording change. The Windows leg notes whether the line appears.
classification_rationale: a claim that the documented log line may not be delivered

trigger: the refusal text changes at a route but still contains 'cursor refused'
summary: The REST and MCP ceiling cases asserted only the substring 'cursor refused' (also quality-engineer). FIXED: both compare the whole message with cursor_error_message(CursorError::kScanLimit); mutation-checked by replacing the route's message with the short literal.
classification_rationale: assertion strength; the model test already pins the literal

trigger: the owner-arm refusal changes status or error code on the MCP tools
summary: Both engine-session sections accepted either a 200 with error 'forbidden' or a 403. The outcome is deterministic (the tool handler answers a JSON-RPC error in a 200). FIXED: both sections require 200, kPermissionDenied and 'forbidden'; mutation-checked by changing the handler's error code.
classification_rationale: a branch-tolerant assertion on a deterministic path

trigger: a later change makes the assign tool read the RBAC store on this path
summary: The case builds its RbacStore on a pool that cannot connect and relies on the tool never reading it. DECLINED: this is the file's existing pattern (the happy-path case directly below uses the same store for the same stated reason) and it avoids a second live Postgres connection per case.
classification_rationale: test-fixture style shared with the neighbouring case

trigger: the non-engine principal-kind literal changes
summary: The harness defaults to principal_kind 'human' and the predicate test pins only 'engine'. The reporter noted the harness as clean and existing cases as unchanged. DECLINED: no defect to fix.
classification_rationale: an observation, not a defect

trigger: a client reads the OpenAPI document for the roles DELETE responses
summary: The OpenAPI entry for the roles DELETE lists no 403. DECLINED: none of the three roles operations (GET, POST, DELETE) lists a 403, before or after this change, so adding one to DELETE alone would make the siblings disagree; the manual is the source for the refusal text.
classification_rationale: pre-existing shape shared by the three sibling operations

trigger: none (style)
summary: The added spdlog and <atomic> includes follow a project header, the reverse of the documented order. DECLINED: the file's own first include block is already project headers then the standard library, so the added lines match the surrounding code; reordering only the new lines would leave the file inconsistent and the Windows block cannot be compiled on the authoring host.
classification_rationale: style; matches the file's existing order

trigger: none (style)
summary: NoReparseOpen's enumerators are lower case while CursorError uses a k prefix. DECLINED: the sibling status enums in agents/shared are lower case (BoundedReadStatus {ok, absent, denied, error} in win_bounded_file_read.hpp, WmiReadOutcome, smbios Status), and the conventions text covers constants, not enumerators.
classification_rationale: style; matches the directory's existing enums

trigger: a registered JVM home whose release name carries a stream suffix
summary: drive_relative_name does not refuse a name with a stream suffix. ACCEPTED, no change: the earlier path-based open accepted the same name, the result is a regular disk file below the root read under the same size bound, and confinement is unaffected.
classification_rationale: behaviour unchanged from before; defence in depth only

trigger: a client pages a sparse wide-scope result past the ceiling
summary: The ceiling refusal has no counter or log, the same as the two existing cursor refusals; the request counter by status and the message text are the signals. RECORDED, no change: consistent with the existing refusals.
classification_rationale: diagnosability only; the message names both bounds

trigger: a session class the owner arm now refuses calls a REST roles route
summary: The REST owner-arm refusals write no audit row while the MCP twins write a denied row (also compliance-officer F1). Pre-existing on REST; this change widens the refused population. To be filed as a public follow-up issue after the PR (an audit gap, not a weakness in the control); the refusal cause (d6) belongs in the same change.
classification_rationale: audit parity between the two transports

trigger: one JVM home whose path draws an invalid-parameter status from the open
summary: The once-per-process warning also fires for a path-shaped invalid-parameter status, so it can be spent before a real unsupported build is met, and there is no metric (also unhappy-path UP-8). RECORDED, no change: the log text already names both causes, every such read still fails closed as release_unreadable, and the Windows leg checks that the line appears once on a rejecting build.
classification_rationale: diagnosability only; rows are never wrong

trigger: the group store cannot be read while a real owner calls a roles route or the token mint
summary: get_group_roles returns no rows on a degraded read, so the owner arm denies with 403 instead of 503. RECORDED, no change: the arm had this shape before the change (an empty vector denies), it fails closed, and the seven sites inherit it unchanged.
classification_rationale: a refusal where a retryable error would be more precise; nothing is granted

trigger: an authenticated caller presents a cursor whose skip is at the ceiling
summary: The cursor is opaque and unauthenticated, so a caller with a matching filter fingerprint can present any skip up to the ceiling. RECORDED, no change: one bounded OFFSET per request, the post-filter still drops out-of-scope rows, and this change replaces an unbounded value with the bound.
classification_rationale: residual cost inside the new bound

trigger: a narrow-scope caller pages a sparse wide-scope listing, or continues an export
summary: The encoder does not clamp, so the server can issue a cursor it refuses on the next call. RECORDED, no change: this is the owner's chosen ceiling behaviour; the refusal is a visible 400 with an actionable message, never a silent end, and the three manuals state it. A redesign of the wide-scope walk is carried as a separate follow-up.
classification_rationale: disclosed behaviour of the chosen bound

trigger: a fleet administrator removes the last owner row of a group
summary: A group with no owner row is reachable only through the fleet-wide arm, as before; the owner arm cannot remove an owner row, so it cannot cause this. RECORDED, no defect.
classification_rationale: an observation, not a defect

trigger: an engine or MCP-tier session calls a roles route
summary: All seven sites traced: REST sites pass kRest, MCP sites pass kMcp, and each refused class is refused before any store read. RECORDED, no defect.
classification_rationale: a confirmation, not a defect

trigger: a package whose maintainer or vendor text contains tabs
summary: The row survives a tab in the free-text fields; the two disclosed residuals stand (a newline in free text, a tab in an early rpm tag). RECORDED, no change: both residuals are the owner's accepted and documented ones.
classification_rationale: the disclosed residuals, restated

trigger: package metadata with a very long line
summary: split_tabs is linear in line length and relies on the existing upstream per-line and per-collect caps, which the reporter did not read. RECORDED, no change: nothing in this change alters those caps.
classification_rationale: a hypothesis about code outside the change

trigger: a registered JVM home with a doubled separator or a '.' / '..' segment
summary: Such a home was normalised by the earlier path-based open and now reads as release_unreadable (the row is kept with its registry tag). RECORDED, no change: failing closed is intended, and agents/plugins/runtimes/README.md caveat 5 already says a name with a '.', '..' or empty segment reads as unreadable.
classification_rationale: intended and already documented

trigger: a refused owner-arm request on REST
summary: A refused owner-arm action leaves a denied audit row on MCP and none on REST. Pre-existing; the change widens the refused population on REST. Owed as a public follow-up issue after the PR (an audit gap, not a weakness in the control).
classification_rationale: audit completeness; no data or authority effect

trigger: none (style)
summary: The header repeats a few NT constants and a typedef that confined_fs_win.cpp also declares. DECLINED: deliberate, stated in the header banner, and already ruled at the over-engineering gate.
classification_rationale: deliberate duplication recorded in the banner
